The substance of the SRO layer is in FINRA Rule 3310/CAB 331. Thus the full broker-dealer pillars duty is assembled only by reading 31-usc-5318, 31-cfr-1023, and FINRA-3310/FINRA-CAB-331 together.

findings.title: Bank pillars content assembled only across 5318(h), 5318(l), sector CFR, and CIP rule
findings.description: The full bank program-establishment obligation is scattered: 31 U.S.C. 5318(h) supplies the base program duty; 31 U.S.C. 5318(l) plus 31 CFR 1020.220 supply the mandatory CIP component; the banking-agency rule (e.g., 12 CFR 21.21) supplies the four pillars and cross-incorporates CIP; and §§1010.610/1010.620 supply the due-diligence-program components. No single instrument states the complete bank pillars obligation; it must be assembled by reading 31-usc-5318, 12-cfr-21-occ, 31-cfr-1020, and 31-cfr-1010 together.

findings.title: Obsolete '90-day/July 24, 2002' MSB program-implementation deadline retained in current rule text
findings.description: 31 CFR 1022.210 (O13) still carries the original compliance deadline: 'on or before the later of July 24, 2002, and the end of the 90-day period beginning on the day following the date the business is established.' findings.title: AML/CFT national priorities published 2021 but not updated within statutory four-year cycle by pinned 2026 date
findings.description: 31 U.S.C. 5318(h)(4) (and AMLA) require the Secretary to update the AML/CFT priorities 'not less frequently than once every 4 years.' fincen-amlcft-national-priorities is dated June 30, 2021 and the item's own notes flag that, as of the pinned 2026 date, the priorities are more than four years old and have not been refreshed. The published priorities are thus superseded-in-substance by the statutory update obligation yet remain the operative published priorities.

findings.title: MSB agent-allocation clause permits allocating responsibility yet imposes non-relievable sole responsibility
findings.description: 31 CFR 1022.210 contains an internal tension between two duties: O14 permits an agent-only MSB and its principal to 'by agreement allocate between them responsibility for development of policies, procedures, and internal controls,' while O15 provides that 'Each money services business shall remain solely responsible for implementation of the requirements' and that nothing relieves any MSB of its obligation. FinCEN guidance (fincen-guid-existing-program-rule-obligations) reinforces the non-relievable duty ('neither the agent nor the principal can avoid liability... by pointing to a contract'). The permissive allocation duty and the non-relievable sole-responsibility duty impose incompatible expectations on the same actors as to who bears program responsibility.

Each money services business shall remain solely responsible for implementation of the requirements set forth in this section, and nothing in this paragraph (d)(1) relieves any money services business from its obligation to establish and maintain an effective anti-money laundering program.

Moreover, each MSB remains independently and wholly responsible for implementing adequate AML program requirements.7 Accordingly, neither the agent nor the principal can avoid liability for failing to establish and maintain an effective AML program by pointing to a contract assigning this responsibility to another party (whether the agent or principal).

findings.title: Divergent 'account' definitions between bank CIP rule and broker-dealer CIP rule
findings.description: The term 'Account' is defined materially differently for the same CIP pillar across sectors. In 31-cfr-1020 (banks), 'Account' means a formal banking relationship (deposit/credit/safe-deposit/trust, etc.) with enumerated exclusions. In 31-cfr-1023 (broker-dealers), 'Account' means a formal relationship with a broker-dealer to effect securities transactions and hold securities/assets. The definitions reflect different covered relationships for the identical CIP program element.

locations.quote: Account means a formal banking relationship established to provide or engage in services, dealings, or other financial transactions including a deposit account, a transaction or asset account, a credit account, or other extension of credit.

Account means a formal relationship with a broker-dealer established to effect transactions in securities, including, but not limited to, the purchase or sale of securities and securities loaned and borrowed activity, and to hold securities or other assets for safekeeping or as collateral.

findings.title: CIP identity-verification timing differs between bank rule and broker-dealer rule
findings.description: For the same CIP program pillar, the timing threshold for verifying customer identity differs by sector. The bank rule (31-cfr-1020, OB-1020.220-a2ii) requires verification 'within a reasonable time after the account is opened.' The broker-dealer rule (31-cfr-1023, OBL-13) requires verification 'within a reasonable time before or after the customer's account is opened.' The added 'before' window is a scope/threshold mismatch for the identical CIP verification requirement.

The CIP must contain procedures for verifying the identity of each customer, using information obtained in accordance with paragraph (a)(2)(i) of this section, within a reasonable time before or after the customer's account is opened.
